doc.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024

title: Riding in Woody Herman's Corvette
summary: Hal rode with Woody because others avoided him, and drove the Corvette with Don Rader on one-nighters.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Per week. And in the section when I was there it was Bill Chase, myself, Gerry Lamy, Don Rader, and John Bennett and we were the trumpet section. And we all got — I think I finally got $150 but I used to ride with Woody you know. Because at that time when we were on the road here on the east coast we’d go to motels or mainly hotels in the city and sleep. That was where we ended up all the time. And we could get a hotel room for two guys each, about $4 and $5 apiece for the room, and sometimes it might be $5 or $6. Well nobody wanted to travel with Woody. Woody had a 1960 Corvette. And all the guys, you know back then they all turned on, we even had a couple of junkies in the band. And so anyway I rode with Woody because nobody wanted to ride with Woody because then they couldn’t turn on. So I was the clean little young kid because I was the youngest one in the band, I rode with Woody and he was a sweetheart. And any time we went over I think it was 250 miles on a one-nighter he would fly and he’d give me the

keys to the Corvette. And I’d have Don Rader come with me. Here we are — Don is maybe barely 5’ tall, and I’m maybe 5’7” at best. So we’d pull up the Corvette into like a West Virginia gas station and these guys in coveralls are leaning their chairs against the front of the gas station just like you’d see in the movies. And pretty soon they got up and they’d walk around the car and the engine would come up so they could check the oil. There was about three guys looking in the engine. And here’s two young guys — I was I think 25 and Don was I think — well Don was just about three months younger than me — six months. So you know we made an impression. But it was a lot of fun and the fact that nobody wanted to ride with Woody and I did, it was just fun for me.
I can imagine you at the gas station, the guy’s going, “What are you all doing here?” “Well we play with Woody Herman.” They’d go like, “What’s a Woody Herman?”
